title: Human review and objective calibration
summary: Human interpretation is explicit evidence, not an overwrite of model output. Pairwise preference judgements can test whether a numerical objective orders real outputs in a way reviewers actually prefer.
authority: Executable dev4 MLReview source/tests are authoritative. The recovered-audio 18/40 artefact weights remain experimental until calibrated.
invariants: Model output, human review decision and policy action are distinct objects.
Review decisions remain historical evidence even after a case is reopened.
Review/calibration state can be rolled back, rolled forward and branched like other driveable ML state.
UNDECIDABLE is first-class; reviewers are not forced into false pairwise preferences.
Objective calibration reports agreement evidence but does not silently bless or refit weights.
Calibration thresholds are explicit policy and can fail closed.
procedure: Present candidate pairs and record MLPreferenceJudgement evidence.
Build MLObjectiveCalibrationReport from the same declared MLObjective and candidate scores.
Inspect comparable, undecidable, concordant and discordant counts plus agreement rate.
If inadequate, fork the scoring policy and replay retained evidence rather than rewriting history.

provenance.claim: Branchable review cases, pairwise preference evidence and objective calibration.
Regression proves review history, reopen semantics and calibration qualification.
Policy for perceptual calibration and held-out future fitting discipline.
